newsitem.title: USA: Publisher Little, Brown to stay in Boston - paper.
newsitem.headline: Publisher Little, Brown to stay in Boston - paper.

text.p: Little, Brown and Co, which has put its historic Beacon Hill headquarters in Boston up for sale, plans to move to 2-3 Center Plaza, a step interpreted as a sign it will stay in Boston, Boston Globe reported Thursday.

The company has been restructing by scaling back its children's book division and selling its professional book business to a Dutch publisher. And the publisher also is getting ready to move its distribution sites from Waltham and Mansfield to Indiana next year, laying off 200 workers, according to the paper.
These cutbacks had triggered speculation that the company would move its headquarters to New York City to be closer to its parent, Time Warner Inc, according to the Globe.

Little, Brown, which has 260 employees in four locations in Boston and Waltham, signed a 10-year lease at the new building. It is seeking to sell its landmark offices at 34 Beacon Street and 41 Mount Vernon Street on Beacon Hill for $5 million, the paper added.
